mainTopic: Does רבי hold of מוקצה, and does רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון or רבי יהודה? The candelabrum and its fixed place
overview: רבי is asked whether unripe dates are מוקצה according to רבי שמעון, and he answers that for רבי שמעון only dried figs and raisins are מוקצה. The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא about desert animals on יום טוב, where רבי seems to hold of מוקצה. It gives three answers. Then the גמרא turns to the הלכה. רבה בר בר חנה reports that רבי יוחנן said 'they said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון'. That report is tested against רבי יוחנן's ruling about a hen's roost, which is explained through a series of narrower cases. A later report from רב יצחק says רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה. רב יוסף explains that 'אמרו' meant רבי יוחנן was only quoting others. אביי brings the story of a fallen candelabrum as earlier proof, but רב יוסף answers that a candelabrum is forbidden even for רבי שמעון because it has a fixed place. אביי then begins a challenge from a groom's canopy, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is the status of unripe dates for רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: A question is asked: according to רבי שמעון, are unripe dates left to ripen considered מוקצה on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Unripe dates: according to רבי שמעון, what is their status?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone (רבי's son, in the surrounding text) asks רבי whether unripe dates that were put away to ripen count as מוקצה according to רבי שמעון. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is known for being lenient about מוקצה. Unripe dates are hard to eat until they ripen, so a person might have mentally set them aside. The question is whether that is enough to make them מוקצה even for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Unripe dates, put in baskets to ripen
What is [the law]? A formula for asking a question

phrases.english: Unripe dates,
phrases.notes: Dates that are not yet ripe and are hard to eat until they ripen.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, what is [their status]?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section of the sugya
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether unripe dates set aside to ripen are מוקצה according to רבי שמעון

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, only dried figs and raisins are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that רבי שמעון has no מוקצה except dried figs and raisins. So unripe dates are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to רבי שמעון there is no מוקצה except dried figs and raisins alone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that for רבי שמעון, the only things that are מוקצה are dried figs and raisins, so unripe dates are not מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dried figs and raisins are put out to dry, and during the drying they pass through a stage where they are not fit to eat. Because of that, the person clearly pushed them out of his mind. Unripe dates can still be eaten with some effort, so even רבי שמעון does not treat them as מוקצה. The answer also seems to show that רבי himself is comfortable with a very limited idea of מוקצה, and that sets up the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside. Items you may not move or use on שבת or יום טוב because you did not have them in mind for use

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין מוּקְצֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: He said to him: There is no muktzeh according to Rabbi Shimon
except dried figs and raisins alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אֵין מוּקְצֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Unripe dates are not מוקצה for רבי שמעון. Only dried figs and raisins are.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about desert animals on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: doesn't רבי hold of מוקצה? A משנה says we may not water or slaughter desert animals on יום טוב, only house animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי not hold of מוקצה? But we learned in a משנה: We may not water and slaughter the desert animals, but we may water and slaughter the house animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי does not hold of מוקצה. It quotes a משנה that forbids slaughtering desert animals on יום טוב because they are מוקצה. The next step will show that רבי himself takes part in this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats desert animals as מוקצה, because nobody had them in mind for use on יום טוב. Watering was done before slaughter to make skinning easier. This step only lays down the law. The proof that רבי personally agrees comes in the ברייתא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving water to an animal before slaughter
Desert animals that graze far from town
House animals that stay close to home

phrases.english: And does Rabbi not hold of muktzeh?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן אֵין מַשְׁקִין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַמִּדְבָּרִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: But we learned: One may not water and slaughter the desert animals,
phrases.notes: This is said about יום טוב.

phrases.english: but one may water and slaughter the house animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי לֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of step 2 that רבי does not hold of מוקצה
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that רבי rejects מוקצה (outside of dried figs and raisins)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a recognized מוקצה category of desert animals, and the next step shows that רבי accepts it.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי still has a category of desert animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines desert and house animals. רבי argues and makes the desert category narrower, but he keeps it. So he does hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: Which are desert animals? Any that go out at פסח and come in at the first rains. House animals are any that go out and graze outside the תחום, and come and sleep inside the תחום. רבי says: Both of these are house animals. And these are desert animals: any that graze in the pasture and do not enter the settled area, not in the summer and not in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines which animals count as desert animals. It shows that רבי, even while being more lenient, still agrees that true desert animals are מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says animals that are out from פסח until the rainy season are desert animals. רבי says those still count as house animals. For him, only animals that never come into town at all are desert animals. Since רבי keeps a category of desert animals that may not be slaughtered, he clearly holds of מוקצה, and that is the force of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the rainy season (around חשון)
Open pasture land far from town

steps.confusionAlert: Do not misread רבי as rejecting מוקצה here. He is actually being lenient by shrinking the desert category, but he still keeps one, and that is exactly what makes it a problem.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Which are desert animals?
Any that go out at Pesach and come in at the first rains.

phrases.aramaic: בַּיָּיתוֹת — כׇּל שֶׁיּוֹצְאוֹת וְרוֹעוֹת חוּץ לַתְּחוּם,
phrases.english: House animals: any that go out and graze outside the boundary,
and come back and sleep inside the boundary.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ בַּיָּיתוֹת הֵן.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: These and those are both house animals.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת: כׇּל שֶׁרוֹעוֹת בָּאֲפָר,
phrases.english: And these are desert animals: any that graze in the open pasture,
and do not come into the settled area

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: neither in the summer nor in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אֵלּוּ הֵן מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 3 by showing that רבי personally accepts a מוקצה category
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא in which רבי defines desert animals (which are מוקצה) as those that never enter town

steps.title: First answer: desert animals are like dried figs and raisins
steps.stepSummary: Desert animals that never come home are just as fully set aside as dried figs and raisins. So even רבי שמעון would agree they are מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: These are also like dried figs and raisins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. Desert animals belong in the same group as dried figs and raisins, which even רבי שמעון agrees are מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, there is no contradiction at all. רבי really does hold like רבי שמעון that מוקצה is very limited. But animals that never come into town are so completely out of a person's mind that they fit the same exception as dried figs and raisins.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say. It introduces one of several possible answers

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
these too are like dried figs and raisins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָנֵי נָמֵי כִּגְרוֹגְרוֹת וְצִימּוּקִין דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 3–4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case into an already-accepted exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Desert animals show that רבי accepts a broad idea of מוקצה, unlike רבי שמעון
steps.terutzMaskana: Desert animals fit the narrow exception of dried figs and raisins, so רבי can hold like רבי שמעון consistently

steps.title: Second answer: רבי was only explaining רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: When רבי answered his son, he was only reporting רבי שמעון's opinion. He himself does not agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: He was telling him according to the words of רבי שמעון, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רבי's answer about the unripe dates was only an explanation of רבי שמעון's view, not רבי's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer removes the contradiction from the other side. The ברייתא shows רבי's real view, which is that he does hold of מוקצה. His statement to his son was only a report of how רבי שמעון rules, because that is exactly what the question asked.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold that way

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he was telling him according to Rabbi Shimon's opinion,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattributing the statement as a report of someone else's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's answer to his son reflects his own opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי was only describing רבי שמעון's view. He himself holds of מוקצה, as the ברייתא shows

steps.title: Third answer: In the ברייתא, רבי argued on the רבנן's terms
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, רבי does not really hold of מוקצה. He was arguing that even by the רבנן's view, animals that come home in the rainy season should count as house animals. The רבנן rejected that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: He was speaking to them according to the words of the רבנן: 'In my view, I have no מוקצה at all. In your view, at least agree with me that animals that go out at פסח and come in at the first rains are house animals.' And the רבנן? They said to him: No, they are desert animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. It reinterprets רבי's statement in the ברייתא as an argument made on the רבנן's own terms, not as his personal view. Then it notes that the רבנן did not accept his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer is the reverse of the second one. Here, רבי's answer to his son is his true view (almost no מוקצה). His words in the ברייתא were a fallback argument: even if you hold of מוקצה, at least make the category smaller. The רבנן disagreed and kept such animals as desert animals.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three ways to resolve whether רבי holds of מוקצה. (1) Desert animals are like dried figs and raisins, so there is no contradiction. (2) רבי's answer to his son only reported רבי שמעון's view, and רבי himself holds of מוקצה. (3) רבי's words in the ברייתא were an argument on the רבנן's terms, and he himself holds of no מוקצה at all.
steps.confusionAlert: The second and third answers are mirror images. The second says the ברייתא shows רבי's real view. The third says his answer to his son shows his real view.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he was speaking to them according to the Rabbis' view:
'In my view, I hold of no muktzeh at all;
according to your view, at least agree with me
that where they go out at Pesach and come in at the first rains,
they are house animals.'
And the Rabbis?
They said to him: No, they are desert animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, alternative answer to the challenge of steps 3–4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא statement as a debating argument on the other side's terms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's words in the ברייתא show that he personally holds of מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds of no מוקצה at all. In the ברייתא he only asked the רבנן to narrow their category, and they refused

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reports that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן: 'They said the הלכה is like רבי שמעון', who does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'They said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to the practical question: whose view is the הלכה on מוקצה? A report says רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds there is generally no מוקצה, while רבי יהודה holds there is. Notice the odd word 'אמרו' ('they said'). It will become very important at the end of this section.
steps.whyThisMatters: This report sets up the whole section. Everything that follows tests whether רבי יוחנן really held like רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They said the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון holds there is no מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing רבי's opinion to the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון (no מוקצה), as reported in רבי יוחנן's name with the word 'אמרו'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן forbade moving a hen's roost
steps.stepSummary: An elder asked רבי יוחנן whether one may move a hen's roost on שבת. He answered that it is made only for hens, which implies it is מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? An elder from קרויא (some say סרויא) asked רבי יוחנן: 'May one move a hen's roost on שבת?' He answered: 'Isn't it made only for hens!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the report. A story shows רבי יוחנן forbidding the roost, which sounds like he holds of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roost is set aside for chickens, not for people. Forbidding it fits רבי יהודה's view of מוקצה. That contradicts the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: To move or carry an object
'Is it made for anything...?' (a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא קָרוֹיָא,
phrases.english: But an elder from Keruya asked him,
and some say from Seruya, asked of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
A hen's roost,
what is the law about moving it on Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּלוּם עָשׂוּי אֶלָּא לְתַרְנְגוֹלִין!
phrases.english: He said to him: Is it made for anything but hens!
phrases.notes: Meaning it is forbidden to move.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the report in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He forbade a roost because it is designated for hens, which is classic מוקצה reasoning.

steps.title: The roost had a dead chick in it
steps.stepSummary: The roost was forbidden because a dead chick was inside it, not because of the roost itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A roost that has a dead chick in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. The problem was what was inside the roost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead chick is not food for people, so it may be forbidden even for רבי שמעון. The roost then becomes a base holding a forbidden item. So רבי יוחנן's answer does not prove he holds of מוקצה in general.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?' (introduces a narrowed case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where there is a dead chick in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The roost itself was forbidden as מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The roost was forbidden only because of the dead chick inside it.

steps.title: But one view says רבי שמעון permits dead animals
steps.stepSummary: The dead-chick answer works only for the view that רבי שמעון forbids animals that died. Another view says he permits them, so the answer fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for מר בר אמימר in the name of רבא, who said רבי שמעון agreed that animals that died are forbidden. But according to מר בריה דרב יוסף in the name of רבא, who said רבי שמעון disagreed even about animals that died and said they are permitted, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. There is a dispute about רבי שמעון's view on dead animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון permits dead animals, a dead chick is not forbidden for him. Then the roost should still be allowed. So the dead-chick answer cannot explain why רבי יוחנן forbade it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works out well for...' (sets up a challenge to another view)
'What can be said?' (the answer is in trouble)

phrases.english: This works well for Mar bar Ameimar
in the name of Rava, who said:
phrases.notes: Skip the רב in parentheses and read the name in brackets, רבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon agreed
about animals that died, that they are forbidden.
But according to Mar son of Rav Yosef
in the name of Rava, who said:
Rabbi Shimon disagreed even
about animals that died, saying they are permitted,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By one version of רבא, רבי שמעון permits dead animals, so a dead chick would not make the roost forbidden.

steps.title: The roost had an egg laid on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The roost contained an egg laid on שבת, which is forbidden as נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A roost that has an egg in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new case. The forbidden item inside the roost is a freshly laid egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid on שבת did not exist before שבת. That makes it נולד, something new that came into being. So the roost holding it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg (here, one laid on שבת)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where there is an egg in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן בִּדְאִית בֵּיהּ בֵּיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the dead-chick answer after the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forbidden item was a dead chick.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden item was an egg laid on שבת (נולד).

steps.title: Whoever rejects מוקצה also rejects נולד
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that נולד and מוקצה go together. Since רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה, he also rejects נולד, so the egg should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said: whoever holds of מוקצה holds of נולד, and whoever does not hold of מוקצה does not hold of נולד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the egg answer, using a rule from רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נולד is linked to מוקצה. רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה, so by this rule he also permits a newly laid egg. That means the egg cannot explain why רבי יוחנן, if he follows רבי שמעון, forbade the roost.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that came into being on שבת or יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think נולד is a totally separate idea from מוקצה. רב נחמן says the two stand or fall together.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Naḥman say:
Whoever holds of set-aside,
holds of newly-come-into-being;
whoever does not hold of set-aside,
does not hold of newly-come-into-being!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the egg answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה, so by רב נחמן's rule he rejects נולד too, and the egg would be permitted.

steps.title: The egg had a developing chick inside
steps.stepSummary: The egg in the roost had a chick forming inside it. Such an egg is not usable by anyone, so even רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has in it an egg with a chick inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: the egg was not normal. It had a chick developing in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg with a forming chick cannot be eaten by people and is not fit for animals either. It is like a stone, forbidden even for רבי שמעון. So the roost was forbidden for that reason, and רבי יוחנן can still follow רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg with a chick developing inside it

phrases.english: Where it has an egg with a chick in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִית בֵּיהּ בֵּיצַת אֶפְרוֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A normal egg laid on שבת, forbidden as נולד.
steps.terutzMaskana: An egg with a chick inside, which is useless to everyone and forbidden even for רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A new report: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר רבי יוסף reports that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יהודה, while רבי יהושע בן לוי ruled like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר רבי יוסף came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: A different report arrives from ארץ ישראל. It says רבי יוחנן actually holds of מוקצה. This sets up רב יוסף's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two reports about רבי יוחנן's opinion, and they contradict each other. In this report, the view that follows רבי שמעון belongs to רבי יהושע בן לוי, not to רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When he came' (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzḥak son of Rabbi Yosef came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second report that contradicts the report in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה (there is מוקצה). רבי יהושע בן לוי rules like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: 'They said' means רבי יוחנן was only quoting
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the word 'אמרו' in רבה בר בר חנה's report shows רבי יוחנן was only quoting others. He himself did not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what רבה בר בר חנה meant when he said in the name of רבי יוחנן, 'They said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.' Others said it, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף makes the two reports agree. The word 'אמרו' was the clue all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was reporting what others said; רש״י explains that 'they' were the members of the ישיבה. His own view is like רבי יהודה. So there is no contradiction: he holds of מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is what was meant when he said...'
He does not hold that view

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אמרו' shows quoting, not agreeing. רבי יוחנן's own view is that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, so there is מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a lesson about how to read a report. A single word like 'אמרו' can show that a teacher was passing along someone else's opinion, not giving his own ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: That is what Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They said the halakha follows Rabbi Shimon.
'They said,' but he himself does not hold so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the report in step 15 with the report in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן personally rules like רבי יהודה (there is מוקצה). His statement 'אמרו הלכה כרבי שמעון' was only a report of what others held.

steps.title: אביי's challenge from the story of the fallen candelabrum
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that רבי יוחנן really does hold like רבי יהודה. His evidence is that רבי אסי, רבי יוחנן's student, would not move a candelabrum that fell on his cloak on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Didn't you also think that רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה? Rabbi Abba and רבי אסי once came to the house of Rabbi Abba from Haifa. A candelabrum fell onto רבי אסי's cloak, and he did not move it. Why not? Surely because רבי אסי was רבי יוחנן's student, and רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה, who forbids מוקצה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not dispute רב יוסף's conclusion in step 16. He asks why רב יוסף needed רב יצחק's report and the word 'אמרו' at all: a real-life story should already have shown him that רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic works like this: a student acts the way his teacher rules. רבי אסי treated the candelabrum as untouchable, which looks like the strict מוקצה view of רבי יהודה. So רבי יוחנן must hold like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: he moved it (טלטול, moving an object on שבת)
an object set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
And did you yourself not hold
phrases.notes: Even before רב יצחק's report, you should have assumed this.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan rules like Rabbi Yehuda?
Didn't Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Asi

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רַבִּי אַבָּא דְּמִן חֵיפָא,
phrases.english: happen to come to the house of Rabbi Abba from Haifa,

phrases.aramaic: וּנְפַל מְנָרְתָּא עַל גְּלִימֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: and a candelabrum fell onto Rabbi Asi's cloak,
and he did not move it.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Is it not because Rabbi Asi was a student of Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
who holds there is a prohibition of מוקצה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרַהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף for needing the report of step 15 (and his reading in step 16) to know that רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה, since the candelabrum story should already have shown it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reliance on רב יצחק's report (and the word 'אמרו') to learn that רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה, when the candelabrum story should already have shown it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A student's behavior reflects his teacher's ruling. רבי אסי avoided moving the candelabrum, which suggests רבי יוחנן forbids מוקצה like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A candelabrum is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the proof. A candelabrum has its own special prohibition, so the story tells us nothing about רבי יוחנן's general view of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You bring a proof from a candelabrum? A candelabrum is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes the proof aside by saying a candelabrum is a unique case. The next step brings the source that backs this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי's behavior can be explained without the general laws of מוקצה. If candelabra have their own special rule, the story cannot prove whether רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: you are saying / you bring up

phrases.english: He (Rav Yosef) said to him:
Are you bringing a proof from a candelabrum?
A candelabrum is different,

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָרְתָּא קָאָמְרַתְּ? מְנָרְתָּא שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not prove the opposite conclusion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the candelabrum was forbidden because of general מוקצה, but candelabra have their own special prohibition.

steps.title: Source: רבי יוחנן forbids every candelabrum, even according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש ruled that a small candelabrum, carried in one hand, may be moved, but a large one may not. רבי יוחנן says that only a simple lamp is permitted, following רבי שמעון. Every candelabrum, small or large, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי אסי: ריש לקיש ruled in צידן that a candelabrum carried in one hand may be moved, but one that needs two hands may not. רבי יוחנן said: We permit only a lamp, following רבי שמעון. But a candelabrum may not be moved at all, whether it needs one hand or two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind רב יוסף's answer. רבי יוחנן says that even in the view of רבי שמעון, only a lamp may be moved, and every candelabrum is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes away אביי's proof. According to רבי יוחנן, even by רבי שמעון's lenient view only a plain lamp is permitted, and every candelabrum is forbidden. So רבי אסי's refusal to move the candelabrum fits רבי שמעון just as well, and it proves nothing about whether רבי יוחנן holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions here. ריש לקיש is the one who splits by size (one hand vs. two hands). רבי יוחנן is the stricter one: every candelabrum is forbidden, and only a plain lamp is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that candelabra are forbidden for a separate reason that applies even according to רבי שמעון. That is why רב יוסף could not rely on the candelabrum story and needed רב יצחק's report to know רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said that Rabbi Asi said:
Reish Lakish issued a ruling in Sidon:
A candelabrum that can be carried in one hand,
it is permitted to move it;
one that needs two hands is forbidden to move.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אָנוּ אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא בְּנֵר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: We permit only a lamp, following Rabbi Shimon.
But a candelabrum,
whether it is carried in one hand
or whether it is carried in two hands,
it is forbidden to move it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 18's claim that a candelabrum is different.
steps.raayaObject: That a candelabrum carries its own special prohibition, separate from general מוקצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's ruling in Sidon and רבי יוחנן's statement, both reported through רבי אסי.

steps.title: Why is a candelabrum forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason is for the special prohibition on moving a candelabrum.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question. It sets up the next step, which explains why candelabra are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know the rule that every candelabrum is forbidden, but not the reason for it. The reason matters because רבי שמעון normally rejects מוקצה, so something else must be causing the prohibition.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason that a candelabrum may not be moved even according to רבי שמעון's lenient view.

steps.title: A candelabrum has a fixed place in the house
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both explain that people set a fixed place for a candelabrum, so moving it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: Because a person sets a fixed place for it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the reason. A candelabrum stays in one set spot, so it is treated differently from ordinary objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a candelabrum is big and stays in one place, it is treated almost like part of the house. That is why moving it is forbidden. This prohibition does not depend on מוקצה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: sets a fixed place for it

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:
Since a person sets a fixed place for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A candelabrum is forbidden because people set a fixed place for it.

steps.title: אביי begins a challenge from the groom's canopy
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that a groom's canopy also has a fixed place. He starts to quote שמואל in the name of רבי חייא about how it is treated. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: But a groom's canopy is something a person sets a fixed place for, and שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא: A groom's canopy...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new challenge against the 'fixed place' reason. This passage cuts off in the middle of the quote he is bringing, so the full challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If having a fixed place makes an object forbidden, then a groom's canopy should be forbidden too. אביי is about to quote a ruling that treats the canopy more leniently, which would contradict the reason given in step 21.
steps.confusionAlert: The quote from שמואל is not finished on this amud. Do not guess the ruling yet; it is completed on the next amud.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
But a groom's canopy
is something a person sets a fixed place for,
and Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
A groom's canopy...
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי כִּילַּת חֲתָנִים דְּאָדָם קוֹבֵעַ לוֹ מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of רבה and רב יוסף that a fixed place makes an object forbidden to move.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A groom's canopy also has a fixed place, yet רבי חייא (quoted by שמואל) appears to treat it differently. So a fixed place alone cannot be the reason.
